title: test-skills carries no lore agent profiles, so the opum-workflow reviewer family refuses here
description:
lore agent list reports "agent profiles: none" and there is no .lore/agents/ directory in this repo, while opum-marketplace, opum-doc, opum-fleet, lore-cli and quest-cli each carry implementation.toml, review.toml, verification.toml and documentation.toml.

An opum-workflow:reviewer dispatched against this repo runs lore agent context review and gets a DEGRADED pack: the Profile line reads no agent profile named review; bundle-wide query hits only, the warning goes to stderr, and --json carries profileMissing true. It then stops without reviewing anything, by design, because an ungrounded review is a different and less trustworthy artifact.

Discovered 2026-10-20 while trying to obtain the Stage 1 review for TS-30, which is the leader unit in any case. Filed at the leader instruction: To Do, unclaimed, off the plan, and not built now. Choosing the profile contents is part of the task: each sibling profile pins concept ids from its own bundle, so this repo needs sources selected from docs/ for review, implementation, verification and documentation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The repo carries .lore/agents/{implementation,review,verification,documentation}.toml, each with sources selected from docs/ for its role.
lore agent list reports four profiles, and lore agent context for each role resolves its pinned concept with the Profile line named (no profileMissing) and truncated: no.
lore check reports no error beyond the 11 schema-drift errors it reports on dev before the change (unchanged count).

implementationNotes:
STAGE 1 VERDICT, recorded verbatim by the opum-marketplace worker at the leader instruction. Reviewer: deepseek-flash (a leader unit, 78 turns). Reviewed SHA: bce82f6cfefb03fa8ae3f47eef933dfe1ae5c2cb (opum-ai/test-skills#57; landed as 901f90b). Source file sha256: 400f5664113a36ec19206413a2feb1d74bfa29caa8154b2f016da41429cd590e. The verdict text follows unchanged.

VERDICT: APPROVE

Reviewed SHA: bce82f6cfefb03fa8ae3f47eef933dfe1ae5c2cb (opum-ai/test-skills#57). I read the detached worktree by absolute path (/Volumes/external/repos/test-skills/.claude/worktrees/review-57-bce82f6/); I have no shell, so I could not confirm the worktree HEAD actually equals that SHA — the object I measured is "the tree at that path", not a verified commit.

Statics that DO hold, checked against lore's own source (lore-cli/src/core/agent-profile.ts):
- Shape is schema 1 exactly (ProfileFileSchema is a strictObject, :75-85): only schema_version/name/description/kind/max_tokens/targets/pinned/sources/delegates; `targets` is optional. All four use only permitted keys.
- name == filename stem in all four (:258); kind specialist with no delegates (:297-314).
- descriptions are single trimmed lines, ~210-260 chars, under the 300 bound (:276) — my count, not lore's validation.
- no pinned/sources overlap in any profile (:398 assertNoReferenceOverlap).
- ALL 15 references resolve to real files: pinned are adr/0002 (review, verification), adr/0005 (implementation), index (documentation); sources are adr/0001, adr/0003, adr/0004, adr/0005, epics/sustainable-test-suites-for-agentic-engineering, runbooks/run-the-skill-evaluations, stories/tmx-test-matrix-engine. Nothing missing, nothing misnamed. (a) is satisfied.

(b) Short answer: partly. review.toml pins ADR-0002 (certificates) and carries 0003 (demote-before-delete/probation), 0004 (constitution-plus-policy, tmx gate reads policy+CI evidence, .test-baseline ratchet) and 0005 (stdlib engine, formats). That is good ADR-level grounding for a gate reviewer. It does NOT carry the state-file contract, and it cannot: DEC-213 (.test-quarantine.json / .test-probation.json; a HEAD state file that exists but will not parse is a named violation, a corrupt BASE copy reads as empty — gate.py:11-14,186-227) is recorded nowhere in docs/. It exists only in gate.py's docstring and .quest records; the sole bundle traces are one clause in TEST-CONSTITUTION.md:129 ("gate state files") and one line at docs/stories/skill-evaluation-suite.md:98. So the reviewer gets the contract from the code under review, not from the pack. That is workable, but it is a grounding gap, not a profile defect.

Findings (all MINOR/NIT — none requires a change to these files to meet the ACs):

1. MINOR — .lore/agents/review.toml:6-10, docs/stories/skill-evaluation-suite.md:98. The gate's state-file contract and DEC-213 are not retrievable from the bundle: TEST-CONSTITUTION.md sits at the repo root, outside docs/, and DEC-213 appears in this repo only in code comments and .quest records (0 matches in docs/). If DEC-213 is architecturally significant for this component, the missing record is an ADR under docs/adr/ — an opum-doc/leader routing question, not a fix for this PR. Meanwhile adding stories/skill-evaluation-suite to review's sources would at least surface the prior gate defects (state files, scoping, timeouts, colliding keys).

2. MINOR — .lore/agents/review.toml:7-10 and verification.toml:7-10: specs/engineering-rigor-profiles is excluded everywhere, and the stated rationale ("keep packs selective") misreads `sources`. Pins are mandatory; sources are task-ranked candidates, and the pack fills by ranking until the budget (docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md:43-45,89-91) — an irrelevant source is simply not admitted, so exclusion buys no selectivity. What it does buy is headroom under `lore check`'s agent-profile-capacity, which measures the complete declared set. For the review and verification roles the spec is the bundle's per-level statement of review obligations, gate mode and approval-evidence provenance (specs/engineering-rigor-profiles.md:147-148, 96-112) — the nearest thing docs/ has to a review contract. The runbook's own remedy for capacity is to re-budget up, not to narrow (:196). Judgement call, defensible because the spec is `status: draft`; worth a re-measure, not a block.

3. MINOR — .lore/agents/{review,verification,implementation,documentation}.toml:5. max_tokens (8000-10000) was not swept. The runbook calls the number "its own measurement" and prescribes a 3-4 task sweep with the "no source scoring ≥9 fully omitted" test (agent-profile-operation.md:118-173). The record shows one pack per role; the cited packs (9.7-16 KB) sit 2-4x below an 8-10k-token ceiling, so the ceiling was never exercised, and the task text passed to `lore agent context` is unrecorded — "3 of 3 selected" is a single-task observation, not a property of the profile.

4. MINOR — .quest/completed/TS-34.json:1. AC3's evidence records a count (11) but not the rule names or severities before and after. A change that fixed one schema-drift error and introduced one new finding would read as "unchanged", and the AC's two clauses would be scored on the weaker one. Record the `lore check --json` rule tallies on both refs, plus the exact commands and the resolved lore version.

5. MINOR — .github/workflows/ci.yml: this repo has no lore job, so nothing validates .lore/agents. Reference validation runs unconditionally over EVERY profile on EVERY `lore agent` invocation (agent-profile.ts:130-151), so one future bad reference breaks `lore agent list` and `context` for every role here and nothing would catch it. A `lore agent list` (or `lore check --strict`) step is the durable fix; this repo already pins a Python toolchain for CI.

6. NIT — .lore/agents/review.toml:7-10: adr/0001 is absent from review (it is in implementation and documentation). ADR-0001 is where the engine's home (test-audit/scripts/tmx.py) and the skill boundaries are decided; a reviewer deciding whether a gate change belongs in test-audit or test-ci has to reconstruct that.

7. MINOR — .quest/completed/TS-34.json:1: the To Do record had acceptanceCriteria: [] and the three ACs first appear in the closing commit, with plan and implementationNotes empty (the evidence is in finalSummary, which is fine). Nothing records the criteria as set before the work, which weakens the provenance of AC3 — the one AC that cannot be re-derived.

Credit where due: the writer recorded the one thing it did not check (an actual opum-workflow:reviewer dispatch) rather than implying it, and the finalSummary names the seeds of its own justification (pack sizes vs budgets), which is what let me test finding 3.

What I could not verify:
- AC2 and AC3 rest entirely on the writer's local lore 0.14.1 run. With no shell I could not run lore: I did not see four profiles listed, a Profile line, `truncated: no`, or the 11 errors. Every validity claim above is static analysis of the TOML against lore's source, not a run.
- I could not confirm the worktree HEAD equals the SHA under review (no git access), nor that an opum-workflow:reviewer dispatch grounds from here (outside Stage 1 scope).
- The 300-character and token estimates are my counts, not lore's validation.
- I did not review the quest status transition mechanics (task move + checked ACs) beyond reading the record.
finalSummary: Added the four lore agent profiles under .lore/agents/. Contents were chosen here as a build detail, from the ids in this bundle: review pins adr/0002 (kill-set certificates) with sources adr/0003, adr/0004, adr/0005; implementation pins adr/0005 with stories/tmx-test-matrix-engine, adr/0001, adr/0002; verification pins adr/0002 with adr/0003, runbooks/run-the-skill-evaluations, adr/0004; documentation pins index with the epic, adr/0001, adr/0004. specs/engineering-rigor-profiles (17.5 KB) is left out of every profile to keep packs selective; it still arrives as ranked retrieval. Evidence, run locally with lore 0.14.1: lore agent list reports 4 profiles; each lore agent context returns the named Profile line, its pinned concept, "3 of 3 selected; truncated: no", and a pack of 9.7-16 KB against budgets of 8-10k tokens; lore check reports 11 errors before and after, all schema-drift already on dev. Not checked: that an opum-workflow:reviewer dispatch grounds here; that needs the leader unit.
